subject: Re: DPA redlines, subprocessor list and UK IDTA addendum coordination
messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finora.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: legal@finora.com
Date: 2027-09-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: DPA redlines and transfer questions

Hi Marcus,

Attached are Finora's proposed DPA redlines. Two immediate asks we need to resolve before procurement will push the PO: 1) confirmation you will execute SCCs + UK IDTA addendum (we've flagged transfers to the US), and 2) a current subprocessor list and the process for subprocessor notice/consent.

A few specific asks in the redline: strengthen transfer-impact language (we want a clearer statement of mitigations beyond 'reasonable measures'), delivery of SOC 2 type II evidence, and an auditable export log for cross-border requests. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide those items and a timeline for DocuSign execution? We need to finalize this week if possible — PO referenced is PO-98021.

Attachment: Finora_DPA_redlines_20270914.pdf (PDF, 142KB)

Thanks,
Sarah Jones
Legal Ops, Finora Systems
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finora.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-14T12:45:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and transfer questions

Sarah — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. Quick summary while we pull the artifacts:

- SCCs + UK IDTA addendum: we can accept execution of the SCCs plus a Redwood UK IDTA addendum. We'll propose a short supplement that references our TOMs and includes the UK addendum language — see proposed alternative for the transfer-impact clause in the attached spreadsheet.
- SOC 2 and evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available; we will share via secure Drive link and can set up an NDA gated download if needed.
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessor inventory; we have a standard notice process and will commit to 30 days' notice for new subprocessors that affect Finora's production data.
- Transfer-impact language: we propose replacing your suggested 'shall' that broadly requires specific mitigations with a mutual language describing "technical and organizational measures proportionate to the data and risk" plus a commitment to provide evidence on request. Kimberly has proposed specific TOMs below.

I am looping in Kimberly (security/compliance) and Priyom (legal ops) to confirm the technical evidence and orchestration for DocuSign. If Finora is okay with the compromise language on transfer-impact and the standard subprocessor notice, we can package the DPA and IDTA addendum for DocuSign today.

Attachments: transfer-impact-assessment-20270914.xlsx

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finora.com>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-15T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and transfer questions

Sarah / team — adding the technical POV. Quoting Marcus below.

On transfer-impact and TOMs: we'll include the following set of measures as an annex to the DPA / SCCs as demonstrable controls: encryption at rest (AES-256) with customer-specific KMS keys available on Dedicated and Private plans, encryption in transit (TLS1.3), access controls with RBAC and SSO integration, detailed audit logs (retained 90 days by default, longer retention available on request), and routine SOC 2 audits. For transfers, our standard approach is SCCs + documented TOMs; where UK IDTA is required we add the single-page addendum that mirrors the SCCs obligations plus minimal operational clarifications (e.g., subprocessors list update cadence).

Regarding subprocessor process: we maintain a CSV inventory and publish notices 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors. For highly sensitive subprocessors we can provide additional evidence (subprocessor SOC reports) under an NDA. See attached subprocessor list.

I have attached a CSV of the current subprocessors and a short redline that softens the 'shall implement X' language into demonstrable actions and evidence delivery timelines. Suggest we accept the SCCs + Redwood IDTA addendum, accept Finora's request for evidence delivery, and proceed to DocuSign.

Attachments: subprocessor-list-20270915.csv

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finora.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finora.com, legal@finora.com
Date: 2027-09-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and transfer questions

Marcus / Kimberly — appreciate the fast turnaround. Finora is generally comfortable with the SCCs + the Redwood UK IDTA addendum and the TOMs you outlined. One remaining ask from procurement and legal: a carveout to the liability cap for breaches caused by gross negligence during cross-border transfers and an explicit commitment to provide SOC 2 evidence within 5 business days of request. Can you confirm acceptance of those two items?

If accepted we will route PO-98021 and expect execution via DocuSign. Please send the DocuSign envelope and confirm the person who will sign on Redwood's side. Target signature by 2027-09-20.

Thanks,
Sarah Jones
Legal Ops, Finora Systems
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@finora.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-17T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and transfer questions — DocuSign and final redlines

Hi Sarah — quick update and final package. We can accept the explicit SOC 2 evidence SLA (5 business days for secure access to the report under an NDA). On the liability carveout we can agree to language that preserves the liability cap but excludes damages resulting from gross negligence or willful misconduct related to cross-border transfer processing — proposed redline attached.

I've prepared the final redline and uploaded the DocuSign envelope. Marcus will sign on behalf of Redwood. Please find DocuSign link below and a PDF copy of the envelope. Once Finora signs, we'll return the executed PDF for your records.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/envelope/123456

Best,
Priyom Das
